attributes.definition: The collector's event identifier. This number must be unique among the event IDs within the expedition.
An identifier for the broader dwc:Event that groups this and potentially other dwc:Events.
The principal Investigator of the grant that is funding collection work or more generally the person in charge of the collecting effort (Firstname Lastname)
The name of, reference to, or description of the method or protocol used in acquiring the materialSample.

The device used to collect an environmental sample. This field accepts terms listed under environmental sampling device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO). This field also accepts terms listed under specimen collection device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0002094).

A list (concatenated and separated) of names of people, groups, or organizations responsible for recording the original Occurrence. The primary collector or observer, especially one who applies a personal identifier (recordNumber), should be listed first.  Name separation should use the pipe ('|') symbol
The continent or ocean name associated with this event.
The name of the country or major administrative unit in which the Location occurs.

The full, unabbreviated name of the next smaller administrative region than county (city, municipality, etc.) in which the Location occurs. Do not use this term for a nearby named place that does not contain the actual location.
The full, unabbreviated name of the next smaller administrative region than stateProvince (county, shire, department, etc.) in which the Location occurs.
The day-of-month when the collecting event started. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 31 (validation rule: >=1 and <=31). Use with monthCollected and yearCollected for the start date.
The day-of-month when the collecting event ended. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 31 (validation rule: >=1 and <=31). Use with monthCollected2 and yearCollected2 for the end date.
An identifier for the set of location information (data associated with dcterms:Location). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
Comments or notes about the Location.

The geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a Location. Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. Legal values lie between -90 and 90, inclusive.

The geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a Location. Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. Legal values lie between -180 and 180, inclusive.

The geographic latitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a Location that denotes the end point of a sampling run. Positive values are north of the Equator, negative values are south of it. Legal values lie between -90 and 90, inclusive.

The geographic longitude (in decimal degrees, using the spatial reference system given in geodeticDatum) of the geographic center of a Location that denotes the end point of a sampling run. Positive values are east of the Greenwich Meridian, negative values are west of it. Legal values lie between -180 and 180, inclusive.
A Well-Known Text (WKT) representation of the shape that defines the location.
The depth of bottom as measured in meters where the collecting event took place.
The name of the person entering the data.
A category or description of the habitat in which the Event occurred.
terms that identify the material displaced by the entity at time of sampling. Recommend subclasses of environmental material http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483

The ellipsoid, geodetic datum, or spatial reference system (SRS) upon which the geographic coordinates given in decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude as based. Recommended best practice is use the EPSG code as a controlled vocabulary to provide an SRS, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the geodetic datum, if known. Otherwise use a controlled vocabulary for the name or code of the ellipsoid, if known. If none of these is known, use the value 'unknown'.
The name of the island on or near which the Location occurs. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names.
The name of the island group in which the Location occurs. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary such as the Getty Thesaurus of Geographic Names.
The name of the water body in which the Location occurs.
The name of the landowner where the event occurred.

The specific description of the place. Less specific geographic information can be provided in other geographic terms (higherGeography, continent, country, stateProvince, county, municipality, waterBody, island, islandGroup). This term may contain information modified from the original to correct perceived errors or standardize the description. If you are unsure of the value and will never come across it, add ‘Unknown’, or if you do not currently have the data but will in the future, add ‘TBD’.
The original textual description of the place.
The greater depth of a range of depth below the local surface, in meters.

The greater distance in a range of distance from a reference surface in the vertical direction, in meters. Use positive values for locations above the surface, negative values for locations below. If depth measures are given, the reference surface is the location given by the depth, otherwise the reference surface is the location given by the elevation.
The original description of the elevation (altitude, usually above sea level) of the Location.
The verbatim original representation of the date and time information for an Event.

The horizontal distance (in meters) from the given decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude describing the smallest circle containing the whole of the Location. Leave the value empty if the uncertainty is unknown, cannot be estimated, or is not applicable (because there are no coordinates). Zero is not a valid value for this term.
A decimal representation of the precision of the coordinates given in the decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude.

A description or reference to the methods used to determine the spatial footprint, coordinates, and uncertainties (e.g. GPS, Approximated from Google Maps, Based on locality name search in Google Maps (Ben Morris script) etc.)
The microHabitat, which occupies a smaller area than the larger habitat.
The lesser depth of a range of depth below the local surface, in meters.
The original description of the depth below the local surface.

The lesser distance in a range of distance from a reference surface in the vertical direction, in meters. Use positive values for locations above the surface, negative values for locations below. If depth measures are given, the reference surface is the location given by the depth, otherwise the reference surface is the location given by the elevation.
The month when the collecting event started. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 12 (validation rule: >=1 and <=12). Use with dayCollected and yearCollected for the start date.
The month when the collecting event ended. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 12 (validation rule: >=1 and <=12). Use with dayCollected2 and yearCollected2 for the end date.
Information regarding the permit.
Information about the presence, absence or other basic status of permits associated with the sample(s).

A permit is a document that allows someone to take an action that otherwise would not be allowed. Examples: Collecting Permit, Import Permit, Export Permit, Intellectual Property Rights, Copyright, Patent, Data use, Phytosanitary, Salvage, Exemption Permit, Material Transfer Agreement, Internationally Recognized Certificate of Compliance, contract, Memorandum of Understanding, Memorandum of Cooperation, Veterinary Certificate, Human Pathogens, Genetically Modified Organism, Other
The text of a permit related to the gathering/shipping or further details
A reference to the permit related to the gathering or shipping event

A list (concatenated and separated) of the globally unique identifier for the person, people, groups, or organizations responsible for recording the original Occurrence.  Examples https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097 (for an individual); https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0097 | https://orcid.org/0000-0002-1825-0098 (for a list of people).
Comments or notes about the Event.
The name of the next smaller administrative region than country (state, province, canton, department, region, etc.) in which the Location occurs.
The taxonomic team.
Enter the event time as local time at the place the event happened, using 24-hour format HH:MM (e.g., 08:05, 14:30). Use this field for a single time value or the start/begin time of an event.
If the event has an end time, enter it as local time at the place the event happened, using 24-hour format HH:MM (e.g., 11:45, 16:10). Leave blank if the end time is unknown or not applicable.

The verbatim original latitude of the Location. The coordinate ellipsoid, geodeticDatum, or full Spatial Reference System (SRS) for these coordinates should be stored in verbatimSRS and the coordinate system should be stored in verbatimCoordinateSystem.

The verbatim original longitude of the Location. The coordinate ellipsoid, geodeticDatum, or full Spatial Reference System (SRS) for these coordinates should be stored in verbatimSRS and the coordinate system should be stored in verbatimCoordinateSystem.

The year when the collecting event started. Expected value is an integer from 1500 to 2050 (validation rule: >=1500 and <=2050). Use with monthCollected and dayCollected for the start date; use 'Unknown' if the value is not known.

The year when the collecting event ended. Expected value is an integer from 1500 to 2050 (validation rule: >=1500 and <=2050). Use with monthCollected2 and dayCollected2 for the end date; use 'Unknown' if the value is not known.
Granting body and grant number, can be in a delimited list.
Any notes taken in the field, or a link to those notes: population size, ecological info, etc.
Substrate from which the individual was sampled. This could be abiotic or biotic (host organism).
The earliest geochronologic eon from which the specimen was collected.
The latest geochronologic eon from which the specimen was collected.
The earliest geochronologic era from which the specimen was collected.
The latest geochronologic era from which the specimen was collected.
The earliest geochronologic era from which the specimen was collected.
The latest geochronologic era from which the specimen was collected.
The earliest geochronologic epoch from which the specimen was collected.
The latest geochronologic epoch from which the specimen was collected.
The earliest geochronologic age from which the specimen was collected.
The latest geochronologic age from which the specimen was collected.
The lowest geological biostratigraphic zone from which the specimen was collected.
The highest geological biostratigraphic zone from which the specimen was collected.

An identifier for the set of information associated with a GeologicalContext (the location within a geological context, such as stratigraphy). May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
The minimum/latest/youngest possible age of a specimen as determined by a dating method.
The reference system associated with the latestChronometricAge.
The maximum/earliest/oldest possible age of a specimen as determined by a dating method.
The reference system associated with the earliestChronometricAge.
May be a global unique identifier or an identifier specific to the dataset. This can be used to link this record to another repository where more information about the dataset is shared.
A description of or reference to the methods used to determine the Chronometric Age.
The method used to generate the value of chronometricAgeUncertaintyInYears.
The temporal uncertainty of the maximumAge and minimumAge, in years.
The verbatim age for a specimen, whether reported by a dating assay, associated references, or legacy information.
A description of the material on which the chronometricAgeProtocol was actually performed, if known.
The output of a dating assay before it is calibrated into an age using a specific conversion protocol.
A list (concatenated and separated) of names of people, groups, or organizations who determined the ChronometricAge.
The combination of all litho-stratigraphic names for the rock from which the cataloged item was collected.
The full name of the lithostratigraphic group from which the cataloged item was collected.
The full name of the lithostratigraphic formation from which the cataloged item was collected.
The full name of the lithostratigraphic member from which the cataloged item was collected.
The full name of the lithostratigraphic bed from which the cataloged item was collected.
free text or reference to dating method for minimum and maximum chronomtericAge.

The names (not dates) of the regional and local occupational periods to which these specimens pertain. Use as many names as necessary to fully define the regional and local occupational periods - these can be either temporally or spatio-temporally defined.
The culturally defined region or regions of which this site was a part during the occupational period to which these specimens pertain - spatially or spatio-temporally defined.

The names of the cultural groups with which the occupants of the site would have been affiliated during the occupational period to which these specimens pertain - these are modern names where original culture names are unknown.
Temperature at depth where the coral was collected in celsius (as defined by GCMP; https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-07275-x)
Sea surface temperature (as defined by GCMP; https://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-07275-x)
Identifier for an environmental measurement record associated with the parent collecting event at the time of sampling.
Identifier for the parent collecting event where the environmental measurement was recorded at the time of sampling.

Type of environmental measurement recorded for the parent collecting event at the time of sampling. If supplied, value must match the controlled vocabulary populated from relevant MIXS water package terms.
Numeric value of the environmental measurement taken at the parent collecting event at the time of sampling. Required when environmentalMeasurementType is provided.
Unit associated with environmentalMeasurementValue for the measurement recorded at the parent collecting event at the time of sampling. Required when environmentalMeasurementType is provided.
Comments or notes about the event-level environmental measurement recorded at the time of sampling.
Controlled vocabulary that classifies this GEOME material entity as a primary sample, tissue subsample, or DNA extract within the folded proposal model.
Identifier of the parent GEOME material entity from which this row was derived. Leave blank for top-level collected samples; use it to link tissue to sample and DNA extract to tissue or sample.
Length of the Organism
Units of the length of Organism measurment.
Weight of the Organism.
Units of the weight of Organism measument.
Fixative used in specimen prep.
The official name (or acronym) in use by the institution having custody of the object(s) or information referred to in the record. E.g. NMNH, US
An identifier for the institution having custody of the object(s) or information referred to in the record.
The name, acronym, coden, or initialism identifying the collection or data set from which the record was derived.

The Traditional Knowledge (TK) Notice label tag that appears with GEOME sample metadata serves as a visible notification that there is accompanying cultural rights and responsibilities that need further attention for any future sharing and use of this material.   The TK Notice is intended to be a collective notice and an initiative to elevate recognition of the cultural significance, importance and often placed-based nature of TK. For more information TK Labels visit http://localcontexts.org/tk-labels/  Accepts TRUE or FALSE
The number of individuals represented present at the time of the Occurrence.
The type of preperation of the specimen.
Preservative used on the specimen.
Relaxant used in specimen preparation.
A list (concatenated and separated) of nomenclatural types (type status, typified scientific name, publication) applied to the subject.
The nomenclatural code (or codes in the case of an ambiregnal name) under which the scientificName is constructed.
Photos, videos etc of the individual. From Darwincore: A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers (publication, global unique identifier, URI,DOI) of media associated with the Occurrence.

Any associated publications/references pertaining to this individual or its derivative tissues or sequences. The first place it was published is particularly relevant. From Darwincore: A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers (publication, bibliographic reference, global unique identifier, URI) of literature associated with the Occurrence.]
A related resource that is referenced, cited, or otherwise pointed to by the described resource.
A legal document giving official permission to do something with the resource.
A note that more precise or other information does exist but is not provided.

A list of additional measurements, facts, characteristics, or assertions about the record. Meant to provide a mechanism for structured content.  Recommended best practice is to use a key:value encoding schema for a data interchange format such as JSON.
The name identifying the data set from which the record was derived.
The collector's event identifier.
The name of the person that entered the data.
A unique identifier (legacy) for the record within the data set or collection.
Add boldBIN provided by BOLD for COI barcodes here. For example:  BOLD:AAF0202
An identifier given to the event in the field. Often serves as a link between field notes and the Event.
A field to populate the /specimen_voucher qualifier field for submissions to Genbank. Please refer to the instructions for populating /specimen_voucher at the Genbank Submission Handbook.
The name of the person modifying the record
The reason for record modification.
Comments or notes about the Occurrence. For example: found dead on road
A statement about the presence or absence of an entity associated with the collecting event. Utilize the terms "present" or "absent".

A list (concatenated and separated) of previous or alternate fully qualified catalog numbers or other human-used identifiers for the same Occurrence, whether in the current or any other data set or collection.
An identifier for the materialSample (individual bone, single specimen, individual, or lot).  Within GEOME, a materialSampleID must be unique within an expedition and optionally an entire project.
Identifier of sample that this sample was derived from, if available.

An identifier for the dwc:Occurrence (as opposed to a particular digital record of the dwc:Occurrence). In the absence of a persistent global unique identifier, construct one from a combination of identifiers in the record that will most closely make the dwc:occurrenceID globally unique.   E.g. a darwin core triplet like: MVZ:Herp:100321 or a fully resolvable url like https://arctos.database.museum/guid/MVZ:Herp:100321

An identifier for the Organism instance.  Can refer to a lot or a single specimen or a single individual of the same taxon.  This identifier does not guarrantee that we are referring to a distinct individual. May be a globally unique identifier or an identifier specific to the data set.
A number or enumeration value for the quantity of organisms.
The type of quantification system used for the quantity of organisms.
An identifier of a distinct individual (e.g. all bones within the same associated skeleton would have the same individualID).
A designation of a child projecct within the larger project.
A designation of a child project to the subProject

BOLD Process IDs are unique codes automatically generated for each new record added to a project within the Barcode of Life Database. They serve to connect specimen information, such as taxonomy, collection data and images, to the DNA barcode sequence for that specimen.  BOLD Process IDs consist of a standard format including the project code and sequential numbers, followed by the year the record was added to the database. For example, the first record uploaded to project PROJ in 2012 would be assigned BOLD Process ID PROJ001-12 . This format ensures BOLD Process IDs are always unique in the system, as well as identifying the year the record was uploaded and the original project it was uploaded to.
Voucher URI used for the specimen (assigned by host institution)

The catalog number used for the voucher specimen (assigned by host institution). Typically this field follows the format outlined in the specimen_voucher qualifier of the GenBank feature table and is structured as institution-code: (optional collection-code): specimen_id. Examples and a list of institutional abbreviations can be found on the INSDC page: https://www.insdc.org/controlled-vocabulary-specimenvoucher-qualifier.
A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers or names of taxa and their associations with the Occurrence.

The process by which the biological individual(s) represented in the Occurrence became established at the location. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. See associated list in lists tab.
Comments or notes about the Organism instance.
Comments or notes about the Identification. For example: Distinguished between Anthus correndera and Anthus hellmayri based on the comparative lengths of the uñas.
The full scientific name of the class in which the taxon is classified
A common or venacular name.

The name of a particular individual.  For example, if there is a Kiwi called 'Freddy', we would put 'Freddy' in the nameOfIndividual Field. This is common practice in Mauri culture to name specific individuals. Note that this is NOT the same as vernacularName.
The day on which the subject was identified as representing the Taxon.
The specific nature of the data record.  Examples include PreservedSpecimen, FossilSpecimen, LivingSpecimen, MaterialSample, Event, HumanObservation, MachineObservation, Taxon, Occurrence
The full scientific name of the family in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the genus in which the taxon is classified
A list (concatenated and separated) of names of people, groups, or organizations who assigned the Taxon to the subject.
A categorical indicator of the extent to which the taxonomic identification has been verified to be correct.
The full scientific name of the infraClass in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the infraOrder in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the kingdom in which the taxon is classified.
The age class or life stage of the biological individual(s) at the time the Occurrence was recorded. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
The original description of life stage of individual.
The taxonomic rank of the most specific name in the scientificName.
The month on which the subject was identified as representing the Taxon. Must be numeric to pass validation
Comments about the morphology of the organism.
Identifiers of other organisms which match the mortphospeciesDescription
The full scientific name of the order in which the taxon is classified

The full scientific name of the phylum in which the taxon is classified.  The list of phyla allowable in GeOMe are taken from the Catalog of Life.  In addition, we have added 'Unknown' as an acceptable value
A list (concatenated and separtaed) of previous assignments of names to the Organism.
scientificName as the lowest taxon identified, use TBD if you do not have the information at hand (and update it later)
The sex of the biological individual(s) represented in the Occurrence. Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary. See associated list on lists tab.
The full scientific name of the specificEpithet in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subClass in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subFamily in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subGenus in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subOrder in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subPhylum in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the infraspecificEpithet in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the subTribe in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the superClass in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the superFamily in which the taxon is classified
The full scientific name of the superOrder in which the taxon is classified
Comments or notes about the taxon or name. For example: this name is a misspelling in common use
The full scientific name of the tribe in which the taxon is classified
Identification number (AphiaID) for Worms database (http://www.marinespecies.org/). Provide only the integer identifier, e.g. 217499
The year on which the subject was identified as representing the Taxon.
A brief description of any processing applied to the sample during or after retrieving the sample from environment, or a link to the relevant protocol(s) performed.
Filtering pore size used in sample preparation
The total amount or size (volume (ml), mass (g) or area (m2) ) of sample collected. Here you can specify a FLOAT value, but you must alson supply sampleSizeUnits
The units to go with sample size of sample collected. Choose from controlled vocabulary.

A local identifier or name that for the material sample used for extracting nucleic acids, and subsequent sequencing. It can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. It can have any format, but we suggest that you make it concise, unique and consistent within your lab, and as informative as possible. INSDC requires every sample name from a single Submitter to be unique. Use of a globally unique identifier for the field source_mat_id is recommended in addition to sample_name.

The device used to collect an environmental sample.  This field accepts terms listed under environmental sampling device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO). This field also accepts terms listed under specimen collection device (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/GENEPIO_0002094).

The bioSample Accession number as reported by SRA.  Typically, BioSample data are submitted first and assigned BioSample accession numbers (SAMNxxxxxxxx). The BioSample accession numbers can subsequently be referenced as appropriate when submitting corresponding experimental data to the archival database.

The bioProject Accession number as reported by SRA.  The BioProject is assigned a BioProject accession number (PRJNAxxxxxx) which is referenced when submitting the corresponding BioSamples and experimental data to archival databases.

The content of this term should include no embellishments, prefixes, headers or other additions made to the text. Abbreviations must not be expanded and supposed misspellings must not be corrected. Lines or breakpoints between blocks of text that could be verified by seeing the original labels or images of them may be used. Examples of material entities include preserved specimens, fossil specimens, and material samples. Best practice is to use UTF-8 for all characters. Best practice is to add comment 'verbatimLabel derived from human transcription' in dwc:occurrenceRemarks.
A list (concatenated and separated) of taxa names terminating at the rank immediately superior to the referenced dwc:Taxon.
A reference for the publication in which the dwc:scientificName was originally established under the rules of the associated dwc:nomenclaturalCode.
The unique identifier for the tissue.  This identifier can be assigned either automatically or defined by the user.
A list (concatenated and separated) of the tissue types sampled from this individual, together with any tissue identifiers that were assigned to them
The name of the plate (typically a 96 well plate) containing the tissue subsamples that will be consumed for DNA extractions for projects
The well location in the tissue plate

The catalog number used for the tissue specimen (assigned by host institution). Typically this field follows the format outlined in the bio_material qualifier of the GenBank feature table and is structured as institution-code: (optional collection-code): specimen_id. Examples and a list of institutional abbreviations can be found on the INSDC page: https://www.insdc.org/controlled-vocabulary-specimenvoucher-qualifier.
Alphanumeric barcode given to tissue by storing institution
Institution  name or acronym which maintains ownership of the tissue
Other catalog numbers which this tissue is known by, for example: 2D extraction barcode
Year this tissue was sampled
Month this tissue was sampled
Day his tissue was sampled by
Person sub-sampling this tissue
Container type tissue is stored in
Presersvative of this tissue
A list (concatenated and separated) of identifiers (publication, global unique identifier, URI) of genetic sequence information associated with the Occurrence.
Remarks pertaining to this tissue
Identifier of tissue that this tissue was derived from, if available.
Sample or specimen data can not be ordered/loaned in general, but are visible via portals. Accepts TRUE or FALSE.
In the case where biosamples have already been accessioned into NCBI's Sequence Read Archive, the user may fill in the biosampleAccession number in the form SAMNxxxxxxxx
Unique identifier for this DNA extraction record. This value links extraction metadata to downstream sequence records and should be unique within the project.
Method or protocol used to extract nucleic acid from the source tissue (for example kit name, chemistry, or SOP reference).

The year when the extraction was performed. Expected value is an integer from 1500 to 2050 (validation rule: >=1500 and <=2050). Use with monthExtracted and dayExtracted for the extraction date; use 'Unknown' if the value is not known.
The month when the extraction was performed. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 12 (validation rule: >=1 and <=12). Use with dayExtracted and yearExtracted for the extraction date.
The day-of-month when the extraction was performed. Expected value is an integer from 1 to 31 (validation rule: >=1 and <=31). Use with monthExtracted and yearExtracted for the extraction date.
Measured concentration of extracted DNA in solution. Record as a numeric value and specify the matching unit in dnaConcentrationUnit.
Unit for dnaConcentration (for example ng/uL). Provide this whenever dnaConcentration is reported.
Volume of DNA extract available or transferred, recorded as a numeric value. Pair this value with dnaVolumeUnit.
Unit for dnaVolume (for example uL or mL). Provide this whenever dnaVolume is reported.
Physical storage location for the extracted DNA (for example freezer, rack, box, and position).
Free-text notes about the extraction, such as deviations from protocol, quality concerns, or handling details.
The name (or acronym) in use by the institution having custody of the object(s) or information referred to in the extraction record.

An identifier for the institution having custody of the object(s) or information referred to in the extraction record. Comments For physical specimens, the recommended best practice is to use a globally unique and resolvable identifier from a collections registry such as the Research Organization Registry (ROR)
A URI denoting the extraction catalog number.  This is provided typically by the host institution.
The 2d barcode on the extraction storage location tube
The identifier for the diagnostic procedure.
The collector's specimen number. This number must be unique among the IDs within the expedition.
The nature of the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion.
The verbatim nature of the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion.
The verbatim measurement unit.
The verbatim measurement value.
The numerical value of the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion.
The units associated with the measurementValue.
A description of or reference to (publication, URI) the method or protocol used to determine the measurement, fact, characteristic, or assertion.
The side of the organism being measured, as in left or right
Comments or notes accompanying the MeasurementType. E.g. '75% of epiphysis'
The description of the potential error associated with the measurementValue.
The date the measurementValue was taken.
Type of sample tested: eg, swabbing, blood, skin, liver
Specific genetic lineage detected (if available) NCBI URI (e.g., http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/biosample/xxxxxxx
Genotyping methods used to determine diseaseLineage if present (e.g., whole genome sequencing, ITS sequencing, multilocus nuclear sequencing).
Controlled vocabulary: Bd, Bsal, Bd+Bsal, Other

The number of positive values for a disease test.  Can be used together with individualCount in the Samples entity to determine the percentage of individuals testing positive for a disease. Must be an integer.
Post-sampling status
Result of disease testing: True=Positive, False=Negative, No Confidence=Ambiguous
At time of sampling, presumed cause of death to be diseaseTested, mark [FALSE] if unknown
traditional PCR, quantitive PCR, realtime PCR, histology, Other
Number of zoospore detected. Needed to calculate Zoospore Equivalent Score (ZEscore), a measure of infection intensity (see Vredenburg et al 2010 doi: 10.1073/pnas.0914111107)
The dilution factor is needed to calculate Zoospore Equivalent Score (ZEscore), a measure of infection intensity (see Vredenburg et al 2010 doi: 10.1073/pnas.0914111107)
Cycle number (c(t)) at which the qPCR machine first detects a positive for chytrid ( a measure of the amount of Bd or Bsal present)
Record the diagnostic lab if different than the diagnostic lab listed in the Project details or if more than one are used.
If present, these values may be entered (otherwise it will be calculated from the quantityDetected and dilutionFactor).
Free text field for description of method for determining ageValue

The numerical value or range indicating how old including the unit such as hours, days, weeks, months, or years the individual is a time of death (paleo and zooarchaeological), collection (neoecological), or observation (non-specimen observations).
Unit for the ageValue in hour, day, week, month, or year

Numerical (float) value indicating how old in hours, days, weeks, months, or years the individual is a time of death (paleo and zooarchaeological), collection (neoecological), or observation (non-specimen observations).

The completeness of the materialSample.  Indicate 'whole organism' if the materialSample represents a whole organism.  For any other condition, choose the most appropriate term from the controlled vocabularly. Use the materialSampleCondition field to provide additional comments.
The post-mordem condition or modification of the specimen. E.g. 'burned' or 'medial side eroded slightly'
The reproductive condition of the biological individual(s) represented in the Occurrence.

Experimental factors are essentially the variable aspects of an experiment design which can be used to describe an experiment, or set of experiments, in an increasingly detailed manner. This field accepts ontology terms from Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) and/or Ontology for Biomedical Investigations (OBI). For a browser of EFO (v 2.95) terms, please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/EFO; for a browser of OBI (v 2018-02-12) terms please see http://purl.bioontology.org/ontology/OBI

In this field, report which major environmental system your sample or specimen came from. The systems identified should have a coarse spatial grain, to provide the general environmental context of where the sampling was done (e.g. were you in the desert or a rainforest?). We recommend using subclasses of ENVO’s biome class: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428. Format (one term): termLabel [termID], Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a water sample from the photic zone in middle of the Atlantic Ocean, consider: oceanic epipelagic zone biome [ENVO:01000033]. Example: Annotating a sample from the Amazon rainforest consider: tropical moist broadleaf forest biome [ENVO:01000228]. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

In this field, report the entity or entities which are in your sample or specimen’s local vicinity and which you believe have significant causal influences on your sample or specimen. Please use terms that are present in ENVO and which are of smaller spatial grain than your entry for env_broad_scale. Format (one term): termLabel [termID]; Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a pooled sample taken from various vegetation layers in a forest consider: canopy [ENVO:00000047]|herb and fern layer [ENVO:01000337]|litter layer [ENVO:01000338]|understory [01000335]|shrub layer [ENVO:01000336]. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

In this field, report which environmental material or materials (pipe separated) immediately surrounded your sample or specimen prior to sampling, using one or more subclasses of ENVO’s environmental material class: http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00010483. Format (one term): termLabel [termID]; Format (multiple terms): termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]|termLabel [termID]. Example: Annotating a fish swimming in the upper 100 m of the Atlantic Ocean, consider: ocean water [ENVO:00002151]. Example: Annotating a duck on a pond consider: pond water [ENVO:00002228]|air ENVO_00002005. If needed, request new terms on the ENVO tracker, identified here: http://www.obofoundry.org/ontology/envo.html

The identifier can refer either to the original material collected or to any derived sub-samples. The INSDC qualifiers /specimen_voucher, /bio_material, or /culture_collection may or may not share the same value as the source_mat_id field. For instance, the /specimen_voucher qualifier and source_mat_id may both contain ´UAM:Herps:14´ , referring to both the specimen voucher and sampled tissue with the same identifier. However, the /culture_collection qualifier may refer to a value from an initial culture (e.g. ATCC:11775) while source_mat_id would refer to an identifier from some derived culture from which the nucleic acids were extracted (e.g. xatc123 or ark:/2154/R2).

A chimeric sequence, or chimera for short, is a sequence comprised of two or more phylogenetically distinct parent sequences. Chimeras are usually PCR artifacts thought to occur when a prematurely terminated amplicon reanneals to a foreign DNA strand and is copied to completion in the following PCR cycles. The point at which the chimeric sequence changes from one parent to the next is called the breakpoint or conversion point

The assembly quality category is based on sets of criteria outlined for each assembly quality category. For MISAG/MIMAG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities with a consensus error rate equivalent to Q50 or better. High Quality Draft:Multiple fragments where gaps span repetitive regions. Presence of the 23S, 16S and 5S rRNA genes and at least 18 tRNAs. Medium Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Low Quality Draft:Many fragments with little to no review of assembly other than reporting of standard assembly statistics. Assembly statistics include, but are not limited to total assembly size, number of contigs, contig N50/L50, and maximum contig length. For MIUVIG; Finished: Single, validated, contiguous sequence per replicon without gaps or ambiguities, with extensive manual review and editing to annotate putative gene functions and transcriptional units. High-quality draft genome: One or multiple fragments, totaling ≥ 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence or predicted complete. Genome fragment(s): One or multiple fragments, totalling < 90% of the expected genome or replicon sequence, or for which no genome size could be estimated

The contamination score is based on the fraction of single-copy genes that are observed more than once in a query genome. Type of fluorophore (reporter) used. Probe anneals within amplified target DNA. Polymerase activity degrades the probe that has annealed to the template, and the probe releases the fluorophore from it and breaks the proximity to the quencher, thus allowing fluorescence of the fluorophore.

Type of quencher used. The quencher molecule quenches the fluorescence emitted by the fluorophore when excited by the cycler’s light source As long as fluorophore and the quencher are in proximity, quenching inhibits any fluorescence signals.

The number of cycles required for the fluorescent signal to cross a given value threshold above the baseline. Quantification cycle (Cq), threshold cycle (Ct), crossing point (Cp), and take-off point (TOP) refer to the same value from the real-time instrument. Use of quantification cycle (Cq), is preferable according to the RDML (Real-Time PCR Data Markup Language) data standard (http://www.rdml.org).

Whether the baseline value was set by the instrument or manually.
Whether DNA or RNA contamination assessment was done or not.
An accurate estimation of partition volume. The sum of the partitions multiplied by the partition volume will enable the total volume of the reaction to be calculated.

Number of target molecules per µl. Mean copies per partition (?) can be calculated using the number of partitions (n) and the estimated copy number in the total volume of all partitions (m) with a formula ?=m/n.

fields.definition: MIXS: Temperature recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: pH recorded for environmental conditions at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Concentration of dissolved salts recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling, usually expressed as practical salinity units or parts per thousand.
MIXS: Specific conductivity recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling, typically in microsiemens per centimeter.
MIXS: Concentration of dissolved oxygen recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Water clarity/turbidity recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling (for example NTU).
MIXS: Chlorophyll concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Alkalinity (buffering capacity) recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Nitrate concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Nitrite concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Ammonium concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Phosphate concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Silicate concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Dissolved inorganic nitrogen recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling, commonly reported in micromoles per liter.
MIXS: Total dissolved phosphate concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling, commonly reported in micromoles per liter.
MIXS: Total nitrogen concentration recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Water current speed and direction recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
MIXS: Relative chemical fluorescence recorded at the collecting event at the time of sampling.
OBA: The length of a multicellular organism body.
OBA: The width of a multicellular organism body.
OBA: The height of a multicellular organism body.
OBA: The mass of a multicellular organism body.
PATO: The distance around the boundary of an organism or organism part.
PATO: The length of the outer boundary of an organismal structure.
PATO: The distance from front to back or top to bottom of an organismal structure depending on orientation.
PATO: The age of an organism at the time of measurement.
GCMP trait: Height of a coral colony, typically recorded in centimeters.
GCMP trait: First orthogonal width of a coral colony, typically recorded in centimeters.
GCMP trait: Second orthogonal width of a coral colony, typically recorded in centimeters.
GCMP trait: Diameter of a coral colony, typically recorded in centimeters.
GCMP trait: Estimated percent of coral colony tissue lost.
Estimated percent of the individual or colony affected by observed disease.
Number of positive values for a disease test.
Quantity of target detected (for example zoospore count).
Type of sample tested (for example swabbing, blood, skin, liver).
Specific genetic lineage detected (if available).
Genotyping method used to determine disease lineage when present (for example whole genome sequencing, ITS sequencing, multilocus nuclear sequencing).
Disease target tested (for example Bd, Bsal, Bd+Bsal, Other).
Post-sampling status of the specimen associated with the diagnostic record.
Result of disease testing (for example positive, negative, ambiguous).
Whether disease tested is presumed to be a cause of death at sampling time.
Diagnostic method used (for example traditional PCR, qPCR, realtime PCR, histology).
Dilution factor used for diagnostics and downstream ZEscore calculations.
PCR cycle threshold/time at first positive detection.
Diagnostic laboratory responsible for the assay result.
Zoospore Equivalent Score (ZEscore), measured or derived from quantity detected and dilution factor.
Name of any observed disease present on the organism or colony.
